cards.english: Fresh bread smells wonderful.
Autumn will arrive in September.
Grandpa tells an interesting story.
What a magnificent building!
A calm sea looks wonderful.
What a clean window!
What a beautiful letter!
I'm cold, close the window.
cards.existing: Impersonal expressions of feeling/state always use dative: `мне холодно (mne kholodno)/тепло/грустно/весело/больно`. The person experiencing goes in dative.

cards.english: Father liked the new restaurant.
cards.existing: `Нравиться` (Nravit'sya) flips the subject and object: `Мне нравится книга` literally = 'to-me appeals book' = 'I like the book'. The thing liked is the grammatical subject.

cards.english: Brother needs a new phone.
She is writing a long letter.
I have no time to talk right now.
cards.existing: Dative pronouns: мне (mne)/тебе/ему/ей/нам/вам/им. Used for the recipient ('to me'), age ('I'm 20 = мне 20'), and impersonal feeling ('I'm cold = мне холодно').

cards.english: Big cities have many problems.
Grandmother felt ill yesterday evening.
The last bus leaves at eleven.
We moved to a new apartment.
A quiet night fell upon the city.
A new house stands on the corner.
An old house stands on the corner.
There is a big park on the corner.
A small table stands in the corner.
My friend is standing on the corner.
Sad music is playing from the window.
We are talking about an interesting movie.
Welcome, please come in.
A big dog is running through the park.
cards.existing: Walking vs vehicle: `идти (idti)/ходить` for on foot, `ехать/ездить` for any vehicle. Russian distinguishes how you move, English doesn't.

cards.english: I am bringing a fresh newspaper to father.
Hi, how are you?

cards.target: Дети моют грязную посуду после обеда.
cards.english: Children wash dirty dishes after lunch.

cards.target: Старая улица очень важна для меня.
cards.english: An old street is very important to me.

cards.target: Эта песня очень важна для меня.
cards.english: This song is very important to me.

cards.target: Маленькая школа очень важна для меня.
cards.english: A small school is very important to me.

cards.target: Красивая семья очень важна для меня.
cards.english: A beautiful family is very important to me.
Family is very important to me.

cards.target: До свидания, надеюсь скоро увидимся снова!
cards.english: Goodbye, I hope to see you again soon!
cards.existing: -ся can mean "each other": встречаться (vstrechatsya = meet each other), целоваться (tselovatsya = kiss each other).

cards.target: Извините, не подскажете, как вас зовут?
cards.english: Excuse me, could you tell me your name?
cards.existing: Compare: `Я Олег` (I'm Oleg – short intro) vs `Меня зовут Олег` (My name is Oleg – full formal intro). Both work, second is more polite.

cards.target: Он встретил старого друга на улице.
cards.english: He met an old friend on the street.
Brother rarely helps a friend.

cards.target: Без хорошего образования трудно найти работу.
cards.english: Without a good education it's hard to find work.

cards.target: Спасибо за помощь, вы очень добры.
cards.english: Thank you for your help, you are very kind.
cards.existing: `Вы` (vy) is both the formal singular and the plural. Verbs always conjugate as plural with `вы`. Capital `Вы` in letters is polite.

cards.target: Мы ждём автобус уже двадцать минут.
cards.english: We've been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.

cards.target: Я знаю этого человека очень давно.
cards.english: I've known this person for a very long time.

cards.target: Дети рисуют большую картину на стене.
cards.english: Children are drawing a big picture on the wall.

cards.target: Они переехали в Москву пять лет назад.
cards.english: They moved to Moscow five years ago.

cards.target: Здравствуйте, я записался на приём к врачу.
cards.english: Hello, I made an appointment with the doctor.

cards.target: Врач принимает пациентов с утра до вечера.
cards.english: The doctor sees patients from morning to evening.

cards.target: Врач принимает пациентов с утра до обеда.
cards.english: The doctor sees patients from morning until lunch.

cards.target: Подождите здесь, я скоро вернусь с ключами.
cards.english: Wait here, I'll be back soon with the keys.
cards.existing: Use `ты` (ty)-form with friends/family/kids, `вы`-form for strangers, groups, or formality. The plural -ите ending also marks politeness.

cards.english: I study new words.
He studies new words.
She studies new words.
We finally solved the task.
The car drove into the yard.
Mom is cooking a delicious dinner.
The roof of the house is covered with snow.
The window overlooks a beautiful garden.
The blue sky is cloudless today.
He brought the purchases into the house.
I see a tall tower in the distance.
An old apple tree blooms in the garden.

cards.target: Оденьтесь теплее, на улице минус двадцать.
cards.english: Dress warmer, it's minus twenty outside.

cards.target: Я беру зонтик на всякий случай.
cards.english: I take an umbrella just in case.

cards.target: Мы пригласили нового коллегу на обед.
cards.english: We invited a new colleague for lunch.

cards.target: Умная книга очень важна для меня.
cards.english: An intelligent book is very important to me.

cards.target: Спасибо за приглашение, мне очень приятно.
cards.english: Thank you for the invitation, I'm very pleased.
cards.existing: Indirect object goes dative: `Я даю книгу другу` (Ya dayu knigu drugu) (I give the book to friend). English 'to' = Russian dative ending.

cards.target: Она вчера потеряла шарф в автобусе.
cards.english: She lost her scarf on the bus yesterday.

cards.target: Художник всегда рисует картину в парке.
cards.english: The artist always paints a picture in the park.

cards.target: Здравствуйте, мы рады приветствовать вас в нашем доме.
cards.english: Hello, we are happy to welcome you to our home.
cards.existing: Default to `вы` with adults you don't know well. Russians are stricter about this than English speakers – wrong `ты` can sound rude. Wait for them to suggest `давай на ты` (let's switch to ты).

cards.target: Прошлым летом мы ездили на теплоходе по Волге.
cards.english: Last summer we went on a boat trip along the Volga.
cards.existing: Add prefixes for more nuance: `при-` (arrive), `у-` (leave), `пере-` (cross), `до-` (reach). `Прихожу домой` (I arrive home), `ухожу` (I leave).

cards.target: Большое спасибо за вашу помощь, это очень важно.
cards.english: Thank you very much for your help, it is very important.

cards.target: На прошлой неделе журналист каждое утро бегал в парке.
cards.english: Last week the journalist ran in the park every morning.

cards.target: На прошлой неделе мы ходили кататься на каток.
cards.english: Last week we went skating.

cards.target: Привет, как твои дела на новом месте работы?
cards.english: Hi, how are things at your new workplace?
cards.existing: Possessives agree with the owned noun: `мой брат` (m), `моя сестра` (f), `моё окно` (n), `мои книги` (pl). Endings shift by gender, number, case.

cards.target: Удачи на экзамене, я уверен, что ты справишься.
cards.english: Good luck on the exam, I'm sure you'll do well.
Congratulations on your promotion!
cards.existing: Times of day are already instrumental: `утром` (in the morning), `вечером` (in the evening). No preposition – the case carries the meaning.

cards.english: I chose the biggest watermelon.
The eighth of March is International Women's Day.

cards.target: Программист редко покупает продукты на рынке.
cards.english: The programmer rarely buys groceries at the market.
